title: Biomolecules
seo_title: Biomolecules Class 11 Biology Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 9)
standard_text: Chemical constituents of living cells: biomolecules – structure and function of proteins, carbohydrates, lipids and nucleic acids; enzymes – types, properties, enzyme action.
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 11 Biology worksheets for NCERT Chapter 9 Biomolecules: carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, nucleic acids, the bonds that join them, and enzymes, their classes and action. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Macromolecules are polymers of small units.
body_html:
How to think about it

Living cells contain small molecules (sugars, amino acids, nucleotides, fatty acids) and macromolecules (polysaccharides, proteins, nucleic acids; lipids also come in the acid-insoluble fraction). Monomers join by glycosidic, peptide and phosphodiester bonds, each made by losing water.

Enzymes are mostly proteins that lower activation energy by forming an enzyme–substrate complex. They work best at an optimum temperature and pH and are classified into six classes. Cofactors may be prosthetic groups, coenzymes or metal ions.

Example

Bond in proteins?

between amino acids

Answer: peptide bond

Example

Enzyme class that adds water to split bonds?

hydrolysis

Answer: hydrolases

Common mistakes

  • Calling lipids polymers in the strict sense.
  • Saying enzymes change ΔG.
  • Confusing nucleosides and nucleotides.

faq.q: Why do enzymes speed up reactions?
faq.a: They provide a different path with a lower activation energy, so more molecules can react.

faq.q: Which bonds join the monomers of macromolecules?
faq.a: Glycosidic bonds in polysaccharides, peptide bonds in proteins and phosphodiester bonds in nucleic acids.

items.e: Three ester bonds form, releasing 3 water molecules: 92 + 3 × 256 − 3 × 18 = 806.
